new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Crossref live 2026-09-20 returns DOI 10.1515/9783110245851 'Dialectology as Dialectic' (2011-04-15), De Gruyter full text paywalled = access 'login'; the pages A read are the publisher-authorized Google Books preview. I re-read A's scanned extract and checked the page scan themselves (pelkey2011_gbpreview_pages/ and): Table 6.2 p. 276 row 'Bokha 33/21 | 21/55/13/33 | 21/33 | 33/21 | 21/33' and Table 6.3 p. 277 row 'Bokha 33 21 21 33 21' are exactly as quoted; Fig. 6.4 p. 286 has a Bokha panel with toneme rows 55/33/21/13/52 (52 = 0% in all five PNg classes; dominant 33 for *1 50%, 21 for *3 53%, 33 for *H 62%, 21 for *L 71%); p. 287 'Most of the PNg tone classes are split between three and…
new_statements.relation_note: Tone only: Bokha tone-class reflexes /55 33 21 13/ in Tables 6.2-6.4 and Fig. 6.4; Proto-Ngwi five-way tone system background (sec. 6.1.1); nothing on stress, accent or prominence.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bokha is a lexical-tone Ngwi language: Pelkey's own field data (c. 160 cognates) give Bokha's reflexes of the five Proto-Ngwi tone classes as the synchronic tonemes /55/, /33/, /21/ and low-rising /13/ (unmarked reflexes *1>33, *2>21, *3>21, *H>33, *L>21; /52/ absent in Bokha), i.e. a four-toneme system of the Core Muji type; the book says nothing about word stress or accent for Bokha or any Phula lect ('stress' = 0 hits in the volume).
new_statements.exceptions: Tone splits by proto-initial class (e.g. TC-1 *b,*p syllables > /21/; TC-2 *voiced and *prenasalized stops > /13/); DXB dialect of Bokha varies /33/~/55/ on diminutive suffixes (p. 304 snippet); /52/ occurs in Muji varieties only as a sandhi allotone of /21/, /55/ or /13/ (p. 246, stated for Muji varieties in the Muji-PJZ sketch).
new_statements.identity_note: 'Bokha' in Pelkey 2011 = his datapoints Bokha-YBZ (Yibaizu, Dishuiceng, Pingbian) and Bokho-DXB (Dixibei), the lect for which he requested ISO [ybk]; the same author and data underlie Glottolog bokh1237. The tone rows quoted are the Bokha rows, not the Muji-S (Southern Muji, sout2722) sketch of ch. 5; the p. 246 sentence about 'Muji varieties' is from the Muji-PJZ (Southern Muji) sketch and is quoted only as clade-level context.

sources.citation: Gates, Jesse P. 2014. Review of: Jamin R. Pelkey, Dialectology as dialectic: Interpreting Phula variation (Trends in Linguistics, Studies and Monographs 229; Berlin/New York: De Gruyter Mouton, 2011). SIL Electronic Book Reviews 2014-003. Dallas: SIL International. 13 pp.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Secondhand summary of Pelkey 2011: 'Helpho and Phuza have a four-tone system, while Muji, Phola, and Azha have a five-tone system.. All of the languages, except Azha, have tone sandhi rules. For all the languages contour tones are only a phonetic phenomenon' (this 'Muji' = the Southern Muji-PJZ sketch, not Bokha); for the Muji clade (nine languages incl. Bokha) it summarises the Proto-Ngwi checked-tone 'mirrored merger' (*H > /33/ after *[+continuant], /21/ after *[-continuant]; *L the reverse). The words stress / accent / prominence do not occur anywhere in the review. Nothing Bokha-specific…

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.note: Bokha is datapoint YBZ ('Bokha: Pingbian County, Dishuiceng, Yibaizu') in the datapoint list, clade table and one cognate remark in sec. 4.6 (Muji meso-clade); the phonology-in-brief sections cover Phola, Phuza, Southern Muji, Hlepho Phowa and Azha only; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the book. SILENT.
